reference_site.name: Jezero crater delta
reference_site.citation: Mars 2020 Perseverance landing site (Jezero crater western delta)

target.citation: Mars Climate Database v6.2 web interface (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology average solar scenario, 18.44N 77.45E, 10 m above surface, all Ls (0-345 by 15) x all local times; retrieved 2026-11-15: water vapour column annual mean 0.0126 kg/m2 (about 12.6 precipitable micrometres), volume mixing ratio annual mean 1.3e-4; no liquid precipitation in the present-day Mars climate; target = driest end of the Earth population (p* = 0)
Haberle, R. M. et al. (2001) On the possibility of liquid water on present-day Mars. J. Geophys. Res. 106, doi:10.1029/2000JE001360 (surface liquid water at most transient; evaporation limits it)

criteria.justification: Liquid precipitation on Mars is zero, which no Earth site reproduces in absolute terms; the analogue is the driest Earth land, so the criterion is a percentile of the eligible population (D-021).
criteria.note: Design mapping: the Mars value (no liquid precipitation, ~12.6 precipitable micrometres of water vapour) lies below any Earth value, so the target is the driest Earth percentile, as for dry_air.

target.citation: Mars Climate Database v6.2 web interface (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology average solar scenario, 18.44N 77.45E, 10 m above surface, all Ls (0-345 by 15) x all local times; retrieved 2026-11-15: water vapour column annual mean 0.0126 kg/m2 (about 12.6 precipitable micrometres), volume mixing ratio annual mean 1.3e-4; far drier than any Earth site, hence target percentile 0 (driest). MCD has no relative-humidity variable

criteria.justification: Very dry near-surface air controls weathering and dust behaviour along a rover traverse; Mars values are far below Earth's range, so the driest Earth percentile is the target.

target.citation: Mars has no vegetation cover; the Mars-equivalent NDVI is that of Earth bare ground

Earth bare-ground reference: annual max of the 2023 MOD13C2 v061 monthly NDVI (modis_cmg builder) over land cells with MCD12C1 2023 barren fraction > 0.9, |lat| <= 52: p50 0.106, p90 0.147, p95 0.166, p99 0.222 (n = 644004 cells). Target max = p90 rounded (0.15); tolerance 0.10 puts the veto (score 0.5) at NDVI 0.20, between p95 and p99

criteria.justification: A Mars analogue for rover operations and remote sensing must be essentially plant-free; p90 over the footprint catches vegetated patches inside the circle.
criteria.note: Was max 0.10 / tolerance 0.05 (data-model placeholder): that vetoed NDVI > 0.125, i.e. about half of MODIS-barren land, incl. Death Valley (footprint p90 0.148) and the MDRS area in Utah (0.149). Vegetated mineral analogs (Lake Salda 0.58, Rio Tinto 0.67, Pilbara 0.30) stay vetoed: this profile targets plant-free terrain for a rover expedition.

target.citation: Jezero is bare rock and regolith with no vegetation, i.e. barren fraction 1 in IGBP terms

Sulla-Menashe, D., Friedl, M. A. User Guide to Collection 6 MODIS Land Cover (MCD12Q1 and MCD12C1) Product, Table 3: IGBP class 16 Barren = at least 60% of area non-vegetated barren (sand, rock, soil) with less than 10% vegetation

criteria.justification: Exposed rock and regolith are needed both for geological analogy and for spectral detection of minerals.
criteria.note: Team decision 2026-11-15 (option B): no veto, tolerance low 1.0, so a non-barren footprint lowers the score instead of excluding the site (barren 0 -> 0.3, 0.25 -> 0.55, >= 0.7 -> 1.0; a tolerance <= 0.7 would score 0 and act as a veto through the geometric mean). This keeps sparse, low-NDVI shrublands as candidates; vegetated sites are still excluded by the no_vegetation veto. Check on MCD12C1 2023, 20 km footprint mean: Atacama Yungay 1.00, Sahara 1.00, Namib 1.00, Danakil 1.00, Death Valley 0.92, MDRS Utah 0.73; Lake Salda, Rio Tinto, Pilbara 0.00 (open shrubland/grassland).

target.citation: Mars Climate Database v6.2 web interface (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology average solar scenario, 18.44N 77.45E, 10 m above surface, all Ls (0-345 by 15) x all local times; retrieved 2026-11-15: diurnal surface temperature amplitude, mean over Ls 84.7 K (75-95 K by season); larger than on Earth, hence target percentile 1 (largest)

criteria.justification: Large day-night swings stress hardware and drive thermal weathering; the Mars amplitude exceeds Earth's range, so the largest Earth percentile is the target.

target.citation: slope p90 = 6.2 deg at 926 m baseline over the 20 km footprint (coverage 1.00), planetary/dem.py (T072), Mars_HRSC_MOLA_BlendDEM_Global_200mp_v2.tif

criteria.justification: Regional slope at ~1 km baseline screens out mountainous terrain before refinement; baseline equals the slope_p90_1km layer output (D-020).
criteria.note: Target = upper bound at the Mars value (as traverse_slope).

criteria.justification: Traversability at rover scale is the top operational constraint for a rover expedition; slopes must be computed at the same 30 m baseline on both bodies.
criteria.note: Target = upper bound at the Mars value: Earth terrain no steeper than the rover site; flatter is not penalised.

target.citation: median RMS of detrended neighbour differences = 0.37 m at 30 m baseline over the 20 km footprint (coverage 1.00), planetary/dem.py (T072), same CTX DTMs as traverse_slope

criteria.justification: Surface roughness at the 30 m baseline describes obstacle density and terrain texture relevant for rover navigation testing.
criteria.note: Target at the Mars value; the existing tolerances (low 0.5 m, high 3 m) define the accepted band, so both much smoother and much rougher terrain lose score.

criteria.statistic: class area fractions over valid pixels
criteria.valid_bands: CRISM summary parameters D2300, MIN2295_2480, OLINDEX3 vs EMIT L2B 0.4-2.5 um; BD1900_2/BD1400 (Earth water vapour) and parameters beyond 2.5 um excluded (mineral_classes.json excluded_parameters)

target.citation: Goudge, T. A. et al. (2015) Assessing the mineralogy of the watershed and fan deposits of the Jezero crater paleolake system, Mars. J. Geophys. Res. Planets 120, 775-808, doi:10.1002/2014JE004782 (CRISM: western fan with Fe/Mg-smectite, Mg-carbonate and olivine)

Horgan, B. H. N. et al. (2020) The mineral diversity of Jezero crater: Evidence for possible lacustrine carbonates on Mars. Icarus 339, 113526, doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2019.113526 (CRISM: Marginal Carbonates near the western delta)

criteria.justification: Fe/Mg-smectite, carbonate and olivine co-occurring in the delta are the geological signature of Jezero's past lake; EMIT can detect the clay and carbonate classes on Earth.
criteria.note: Target from published CRISM analyses (Goudge et al. 2015; Horgan et al. 2020). Supporting T073/T074 extraction over the 20 km footprint (FRT000047A3, FRT00005850): olivine 0.26, Fe/Mg-smectite 0.0058, carbonate 0.0005 of valid pixels; the CRISM thresholds are a project choice, not published values (research.md, T036), so these fractions are indicative only. EMIT cannot detect olivine.

target.citation: Goudge, T. A. et al. (2015) Assessing the mineralogy of the watershed and fan deposits of the Jezero crater paleolake system, Mars. J. Geophys. Res. Planets 120, 775-808, doi:10.1002/2014JE004782 (CRISM: western fan with Fe/Mg-smectite, Mg-carbonate and olivine)

criteria.justification: Aqueous minerals are both a resource indicator and the scientific reason for visiting the site.

target.citation: Mars Climate Database v6.2 web interface (LMD/OU/IAA/ESA/CNES), climatology average solar scenario, 18.44N 77.45E, 10 m above surface, all Ls (0-345 by 15) x all local times; retrieved 2026-11-15: surface pressure annual mean 723 Pa (615-827 Pa)

criteria.justification: Earth surface pressure (~100 kPa) cannot reproduce Mars' thin atmosphere; kept for the analogy-limits statement.

target.citation: NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet (D. R. Williams), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html, last updated 19 May 2025: surface gravity (mean) 3.73 m/s2 (equator 3.69, pole 3.73); Earth 9.82

criteria.justification: Gravity cannot be reproduced on Earth; it affects wheel-soil interaction and is stated as an analogy limit.

target.citation: Martinez, G. M. et al. (2022) Thermal inertia and albedo at Jezero crater as observed from the Mars 2020 MEDA instrument. 53rd Lunar and Planetary Science Conference, abstract 2024: THEMIS (100 m/px) thermal inertia along the Perseverance traverse 200-450 SI units; MEDA in situ 200 (sand) - 600 (bedrock), first 221 sols

criteria.justification: No global Earth thermal-inertia layer exists in the grid; kept to describe surface material and as an analogy limit.

removed_criteria.reason: Low relevance for a rover expedition; Mars wind values are model-only (FR-005).
No automatic global Earth landform classification (delta, paleolake) available (FR-005).
No global Earth dataset of pits or lava tubes (FR-005).

profile.notes: v1 profile. All targets sourced (T036, 2026-11-15): terrain from T072 (CTX DTMs, MOLA+HRSC), mineral classes from published CRISM analyses (Goudge et al. 2015; Horgan et al. 2020), climate from the Mars Climate Database v6.2, gravity from the NSSDCA fact sheet, thermal inertia from THEMIS (Martinez et al. 2022); no_vegetation and barren_ground are Earth bare-ground equivalents checked on MODIS 2023 data (see criterion notes). hyperarid, dry_air and thermal_swing are percentile design mappings of Mars values outside the Earth range. Pending: review of targets, tolerances and vetoes by a second team member ("reviewed by <initials>, <date>").
